summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR4,319 crores and PAT more than quadrupled to INR161 crores; Q2 EBITDA margin 6.9%, up 180 bps.
summary.overview: Electronics Mart India reported a strong H1 FY27, with revenue up 30% and EBITDA nearly doubling to INR369 crores at an 8.6% margin. Q2 revenue grew 19% to INR1,900 crores, with same-store sales growth of 16.5%, a softer quarter after a strong Q1 driven by air conditioners. Gross margin gains were attributed partly to price escalations in mobile and IT products and an extended summer that kept AC sales up in Q2, and management said H2 gross margin should be around 15%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 20% revenue growth and said festive demand had started in line with expectations.

financial_highlights.value: INR384 crores post-Ind AS; INR304 crores pre-Ind AS
financial_highlights.change: +41% YoY post-Ind AS; pre-Ind AS vs INR202 crores
vs 77 days at 30 Sep 2025 and 73 days at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Mobile phones
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue grew 31%, supported by launches; mobile was 53% of Q2 product revenue and 45% of H1 product revenue. Entry-level phones below INR20,000 saw volume declines, while premium segments held up.

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Q2 AC sales grew 52% as extended summer carried into the quarter; large appliances were 41% of H1 product revenue (48% of Q1 revenue).

segments.name: Other categories (Q2 growth)
segments.commentary: Built-in appliances +35%, dishwashers +41%, tablets +52%, wearables +26%. Television sales expected to be flattish against a strong prior-year pre-GST-cut pent-up demand.

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 28% with EBITDA margin up 320 bps to 9.3%. Q2: Andhra Pradesh +24%, Telangana upcountry +17%, Hyderabad city +16%; H1: Andhra Pradesh +45%, Telangana +33%, Hyderabad city +25%.

segments.name: North cluster
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up 45% and H1 up 36%; H1 EBITDA margin rose to 3.4% from 1%, with management targeting South benchmarks.

segments.name: Store cohorts
segments.commentary: 102 stores older than four years earn a 9.7% EBITDA margin; 127 stores under four years old earn 6.4%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% YoY maintained; management expects an additional INR100-200 crores of upside from an early summer in Q4.

Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin guidance of 7.5%-8% reiterated (pre-Ind AS roughly 6%-6.5%); Akhil Parekh's question framed it as 18%-20% growth, 15%-15.5% gross margin and 7.5%-8% EBITDA margin, which management confirmed.
H2 blended gross margin target around 15%, with no repeat of H1 price-escalation gains expected.
FY27 pre-Ind AS operating cash flow guided at around INR600 crores, versus about INR350 crores for FY26.
Store additions of 25-30 targeted for FY27 (9 added so far in H1, 229 stores at period end); FY28 additions expected at 25 or more.
West Bengal (Kolkata) entry: 4-5 stores to open by mid-November 2026; 15 of 22 signed Kolkata properties expected to open over the next two to three quarters.
capex_capacity: Network at 229 stores across 102 cities (222 MBO and 7 EBO); H1 net addition of 6 stores; total retail area about 2 million sq ft.
Central warehousing expanded to 14 locations to support growth.
Kolkata/West Bengal entry progressing; 25-30 staff already on the ground there, with store launches planned from mid-November 2026.
Store additions expected in Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh, Delhi NCR and Kolkata during the rest of FY27.
demand_pricing: H1 same-store sales growth 27.5%; Q2 SSG 16.5%; SSG across clusters ranged from 13% to 40%.
Q2 bill cuts up about 3%; average ticket size up nearly 15% to over INR25,700. Management said bill count is secondary to value.
Festive demand started strongly and was in line with plan, with stock positioned across categories. Early Navratri and pent-up demand last year make television flattish this year.
Entry-level mobile (below INR20,000) volumes declined as prices rose; premium phones above INR50,000 grew in single digits with higher ASPs. iPhone 18 Pro and Duo stock sold out.
Incentive and commission income about INR11 crores in Q2 versus INR7 crores a year earlier (management said other commissions were similar).

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 surprise given the festive shift, and can Q4 margins repeat Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no surprises and Q3 festive season started well; Q4 upside depends on an early summer, but Q4 margins will not necessarily match Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin expansion was from inflation-driven price escalations, and will it continue in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said price escalations added about 150 bps in Q1 and about 30 bps in Q2; H2 gross margin is targeted at around 15%, with no repeat of those gains assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is store addition slower in H1 and what is the outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays were due to properties still being readied, mainly Kolkata (15 of 22 signed properties to open over 2-3 quarters). FY27 target is 25-30 stores; FY28 at least 25.

qa_highlights.question: Why did bill cuts grow only about 3% and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's early Diwali and pent-up demand, particularly in ACs, appliances and TVs, shifted sales; entry-level phones and laptops also slowed. Management said it focuses on value and ASP rather than bill count.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 18% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-opening hiring for Kolkata, a salary revision that happens every 18-20 months, and a rise in minimum wages from INR15,000 to INR25,000 per month drove the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 pre-Ind AS operating cash flow be about INR600 crores, and what was FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a pre-Ind AS operating cash flow target of around INR600 crores for FY27; FY26 pre-Ind AS operating cash flow was about INR350 crores.

risks_watch: Gross margin normalising to about 15% in H2 after H1 price-escalation gains.
Entry-level mobile volume decline as phone prices rise; demand sensitivity to further price hikes.
Q4 depends on an early summer; Q4 margins may not match Q1.
Cluster margins: the North cluster is still at 3.4% H1 EBITDA margin, and stores under four years old run at 6.4%.
Kolkata ramp-up timing and rising employee costs ahead of store openings.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year outlook and festive start, while being measured on upgrades: management kept the FY27 guidance unchanged and flagged that H1 gains (price escalation, extended summer) would not fully repeat in H2.
key_quotes: Even so, with the mobile-heavy mix in Q2 FY27, we delivered an EBITDA margin of 6.9% and improvement of 180 bps year-on-year.
We expect store productivity and margins here to continue moving towards South cluster benchmarks.
But we are looking at a very positive cash flow coming in at around INR600 crores for the whole year, very comfortably.
I think we like to stick to what we committed, but the EBITDA numbers that you are looking at are pre-Ind AS and post-Ind AS.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% held (100-200 bps upside possible from early summer), backed by 9 stores added in H1 with 25-30 targeted for FY27 and Kolkata entry starting mid-November, plus H1 SSG of 27.5%; however H2 gross margin is guided to ~15% with no repeat of price-escalation gains and Q2 bill count fell about 3%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided H2 blended gross margin to around 15% (H1 gross margin 16.4%, Q2 15.4%) with no repeat of price-escalation gains (about 150 bps in Q1 and 30 bps in Q2), and Q4 margins may not match Q1; FY27 post-Ind AS EBITDA margin held at 7.5%-8% versus H1 8.6%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 9 stores added in H1 with 25-30 targeted for FY27 (229 stores at period end, implying roughly 16-21 more in H2), Kolkata 4-5 stores by mid-November 2026 and 15 of 22 signed Kolkata properties over the next 2-3 quarters; FY28 additions of 25+ guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 same-store sales growth 27.5% and Q2 SSG 16.5%, with festive demand started in line with plan, but Q2 bill cuts rose only about 3% and entry-level mobile volumes below INR20,000 declined, so growth is value-led (ticket size up ~15% to over INR25,700).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex quantum disclosed and utilisation not discussed; the store roll-out (25-30 in FY27, 25+ in FY28) and 14 central warehouse locations suggest continued investment, but no fresh capex plan was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said an early summer in Q4 could add INR100-200 crores of revenue upside (about 100-200 bps on the ~20% growth guide), but kept FY27 revenue guidance of about 20% unchanged citing half the year remaining.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 gross margin guided to ~15% versus 16.4% in H1 as price-escalation gains do not repeat, and employee costs rose about 18% YoY ahead of Kolkata openings; North cluster margin of 3.4% and 127 sub-four-year stores at 6.4% are watch items.

rows.label: Pre-Ind AS operating cash flow of ~INR600 crores in FY27
rows.why: H1 pre-Ind AS operating cash flow INR304 crores versus INR202 crores last year, with working capital days down to 61 from 77 a year ago; management says the full-year target of ~INR600 crores is very comfortable versus about INR350 crores in FY26.

rows.label: North cluster margin catch-up toward South benchmarks
rows.why: North H1 EBITDA margin rose to 3.4% from 1% and North revenue grew 36% in H1, with management targeting South cluster benchmarks (South H1 margin 9.3%); this is a stated aim, not a dated commitment.

rows.label: Kolkata / West Bengal store launches
rows.why: 4-5 stores are set to open by mid-November 2026 with 25-30 staff already on the ground, and 15 of 22 signed properties expected to open over the next 2-3 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on the full-year revenue and cash-flow outlook and the festive start, but cautious on margins, saying H2 gross margin would be around 15% with no repeat of price-escalation gains; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, store-addition delays and the bill-count slowdown.
